open_points.subject: R0-89 backup checkpoint for migration retirement
open_points.text: until a checked backup holds the import
open_points.question: What exactly must the backup check establish for a backup to “hold the import,” and what observable result tells the owner that the condition has succeeded or failed before deleting the recovery copy and retiring the VPS?
options: The check proves both the imported records and the store's closed-import fact are present and reports that result
Any successful integrity check of a backup made after the import is enough
Only a tested restoration can establish the condition
open_points.default_guess: Require an observable successful check proving that both the imported records and the closed-import fact are present.

open_points.subject: R0-89 loss boundary
open_points.text: every change after it is lost
open_points.question: After which event are changes lost: after the backup was made, after the store was lost, or after some other checkpoint?
options: Every change committed after the restored backup's snapshot was made is lost
Only changes made after the store-loss event are lost
Changes after the most recent successful backup check are lost
open_points.default_guess: Treat every change committed after the restored backup's snapshot was made as lost.

open_points.subject: R0-89 import recovery inputs
open_points.text: the import's choices include the names, kinds and tax-id answers given for the Customers it made
open_points.question: Which customer decisions must the owner give during import, how are they associated with source customers, and are they part of the import file, the import request, or a separate retained recovery record?
options: Store all project selections, replacement names, aliases, customer mappings, customer kinds and tax-id decisions in one retained import manifest
Embed the decisions in the migration export file
Keep the export and a separate owner-authored choices document
open_points.default_guess: Use one retained import manifest associated with the export and containing every owner choice needed to repeat the import.

open_points.subject: R0-80 one-home rule affected by R0-89
open_points.text: A customer's living personal data — name, contact data, tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF), legal name — and the object's address and identifying characteristics are held only by Registry
open_points.question: Is the personal-data-bearing export and choices copy kept in Bitwarden an explicit temporary exception to R0-80's rule that these values are held only by Registry?
options: Add the vault recovery copy as a temporary governed exception until a checked backup holds the import
Define migration exports as outside the meaning of living personal data
Require the retained recovery material not to contain those personal values
open_points.default_guess: Treat the vault recovery copy as an explicit temporary, governed exception to the one-home rule.

open_points.subject: R0-89 scope of guarantees after restoration
open_points.text: Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering, the closed import — hold within each store's history
open_points.question: Are all state-dependent Registry guarantees scoped independently to each restored store history, or only audit numbering and import closure?
options: All guarantees whose truth depends on stored history are scoped to that history
Only audit numbering and import closure are scoped per history
Each affected guarantee must be enumerated separately
open_points.default_guess: Scope every guarantee whose truth depends on persisted history to the particular store history, with audit numbering and import closure as examples.
